get.summary: Realtime chat hub for API-key consumers (X-API-KEY) — WebSocket, not a REST endpoint
get.description:
The realtime counterpart to the `/portal` endpoints: a SignalR hub authenticated **only** by the
API key. Deliberately a separate hub from `/chat` so the token path and the key
path share no authorization code. **"Try it out" cannot exercise this path** — a plain `GET` is
rejected by the handshake.

### Choose your subscription first
One key, two subscription shapes. The optional
`contactId` on the handshake is what picks between
them, and a connection is one or the other — **never both**:

| Handshake | Group joined | Receives | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `?apikey={key}` | `org-{organizationId}` | every conversation of your organization, both sides of every thread | an operator console, an inbox view, a CRM sync — anything organization-wide |
| `?apikey={key}&contactId={contactId}` | `contact-{contactId}` | **one thread only** — that contact's conversation with your organization | a contact-facing widget, kiosk or app screen, for a person who may have no AeonPass account |

The contact scope **replaces** the organization group rather than adding to it. That is the whole
point of it: a contact-facing client must not receive the organization's other conversations. If
you need both views at once, open two connections.

### Where to connect
This service maps the hub at `/portal/chat`. Public callers reach it
through the API gateway, which prefixes every route in this document — this one included — with
`/api`. Pick the row matching the host you are actually calling:

| You are calling | Hub URL |
| --- | --- |
| The gateway — the `servers` entry above, and what every published integration uses | `wss://{host}/api/portal/chat` |
| This service directly — in-cluster, or a local run | `wss://{host}/portal/chat` |

Using the wrong one fails as a **404 on the negotiate request**, not a 401 — if you are debugging
an auth problem and seeing 404, this is why.

### Handshake
Your SignalR client does all of this; it matters only when debugging. The client first `POST`s to
`…/portal/chat/negotiate?negotiateVersion=1`. Where the Azure SignalR
Service backplane is configured, that answers with a redirect payload — a `url` on the service
host plus a short-lived `accessToken` — and the WebSocket is then opened against **that** host
rather than this one. So the socket you see on the wire terminates at `*.service.signalr.net`,
and the `101 Switching Protocols` comes from there.

### Authentication
Prefer the `X-API-KEY` header wherever your client can set
headers on the handshake — `@microsoft/signalr` can under Node, a browser cannot.

The query form
`?apikey={key}` is the fallback, and this is the one
route in the whole API that accepts a key in a URL: every other portal route requires the header,
which keeps a long-lived key out of access logs, request telemetry and browser history. One thing
to know when choosing it — the negotiate redirect carries the key onward into the Azure SignalR
Service `url`, whereas the header form leaves that URL clean. Both are accepted; the header keeps
the key on fewer hops.

Either way the path fails closed: a missing, unknown or revoked key is a `401` at negotiate, so
no socket is opened.

### The `contactId` parameter
Optional, query string only, and honoured on this path alone. Supply it to narrow the connection
to one contact's thread; omit it for the organization-wide subscription this hub has always given.

It is **validated during authentication**, before any socket exists: the contact must exist in
chat's replica and belong to **this key's** organization. If it does not, the negotiate request
fails `401` — deliberately, rather than either of the two tempting alternatives. Falling back to
the organization group would hand a contact-facing client every conversation in the organization,
which is the leak this parameter exists to prevent; narrowing silently to nothing would be
indistinguishable from a dead connection. So a `401` here with a valid key means the `contactId`
is unknown, malformed, or another organization's.

Note the asymmetry with the key itself: the key may also travel as a header, but
`contactId` is query-string only. A contact id is not
a secret, and keeping it in the URL means it is visible in the one place you debug a subscription
from.

### What the connection is subscribed to
One group, joined on connect, chosen by the handshake — see the chooser at the top of this entry:

| | Group | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No `contactId` | `org-{organizationId}` | the key's whole organization |
| With `contactId` | `contact-{contactId}` | that contact's single thread |

Still no `event-{eventId}` group and no user-id addressing: those are person-scoped views an
organization key does not hold. The contact group is not a person-scoped view — it is one
*conversation* of the key's own organization, which the key can already read over HTTP.

The hub is **receive-only**: it exposes no client-callable methods, on either shape. Sending stays
on HTTP — `POST /api/portal/conversations/send-message` and
`PUT /api/portal/conversations/{id}/mark-read`. Note that mark-read takes no
fields but still requires a JSON body: send `{}` with `Content-Type: application/json` or it
answers `415`.

**Sending from the contact side** is the send endpoint's `sendFrom` field, not a hub concern:
`sendFrom: "Contact"` with a `contactId` records the message as coming from that contact, exactly
as an inbound SMS reply is stored, so it arrives on every subscriber with
`lastMessage.isFromOrganization: false`. Two things a contact-facing client should know: those
sends dispatch **nothing** to the contact (the `inApp`/`inSMS`/`inEmail` channels describe how to
reach the contact, so they only mean anything when sending as the organization), and there is no
contact-side **mark-read** on this surface — `PUT …/mark-read` always records the *organization*
as the reader, whichever way the connection is scoped.

### Server → client events

**`ReceiveMessage`** — a message was sent in a conversation this connection covers: any of your
organization's on the org-wide shape, that one thread on the contact-scoped shape. Either side's
message, from any surface. Not gated on the contact's delivery channels, so a send with `inApp`,
`inSMS` and `inEmail` all false still arrives here. Payload `ConversationPushDto`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | uuid | the **conversation** id — not the message id |
| `organizationId` | uuid | always your organization |
| `organizationName`, `organizationLogoUrl`, `organizationIsSetup`, `organizationEmail`, `organizationPhone` | string / bool | organization display fields |
| `contact` | `ConversationParticipantDto` | the contact side of the thread |
| `lastMessage` | `MessageDto` | **the new message** — body, attachments, sender, timestamp |
| `lastMessage.isFromOrganization` | bool | **which side sent it** — the field to branch on. `false` covers every contact-side message: an SMS reply, a contact's in-app send, and one recorded through `sendFrom: "Contact"` |
| `senderUserId` | uuid | who sent it; same value as `lastMessage.senderId`. On a contact-side message this is the **contactId**, not a user id |

Deliberately caller-neutral: it carries no `unreadCount` and no `isReadByUser`, because one group
push is delivered to every subscriber and those values differ per reader. Track them locally, or
re-read `GET /api/portal/conversations/{id}`.

The push is sender-neutral, so **your own sends come back to you** on the connection that made
them. Reconcile on `lastMessage.id` rather than assuming an inbound event is someone else's.

**`MarkMessagesRead`** — a read receipt, and which direction you see depends on which shape you
connected as. Your own `mark-read` call never echoes back to you; that endpoint returns the receipt
in its HTTP response instead. Payload `MarkAsReadConversationDto`:

| Field | Type | Org-wide connection | Contact-scoped connection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | uuid | conversation id | conversation id |
| `readDate` | date-time | when it was read | when it was read |
| `organizationId` | uuid | your organization | your organization |
| `readByContact` | bool | `true` — **the contact** read your message | `false` — **the organization** read the contact's message |
| `receiverMemberUserId` | uuid or null | null — it addresses the token surface | the contact's linked user account, or null when they have none |
| `contactId` | uuid or null | null | the contact whose thread was read — the value that routed this event here |

So on the org-wide shape this event means "the other side has seen it", as before. On the
contact-scoped shape it is the mirror: your organization has seen the contact's message. Branch on
`readByContact` rather than assuming a direction, and note this is the only channel that delivers
a read receipt to a contact who has **no** user account — `Clients.User` on the token hub cannot
address one.

#### Example 1 — organization-wide, Node (header form)
Preferred wherever your client can set handshake headers: the key never enters a URL, and so never
reaches the Azure SignalR Service redirect.

```js
const hub = new signalR.HubConnectionBuilder()
  .withUrl("https://{host}/api/portal/chat", {
    headers: { "X-API-KEY": apiKey },
  })
  .withAutomaticReconnect()
  .build();

hub.on("ReceiveMessage", c => {
  if (c.lastMessage.isFromOrganization) return;      // our own outbound, echoed back
  inbox.bump(c.id, c.contact, c.lastMessage);         // a contact replied
});

hub.on("MarkMessagesRead", r => {
  if (r.readByContact) inbox.markSeen(r.id, r.readDate);
});

await hub.start();
```

#### Example 2 — organization-wide, browser (query form)
A browser cannot set headers on the handshake, so the key goes in the query string. This is the one
route in the API that accepts that; treat the key as rotatable.

```js
const hub = new signalR.HubConnectionBuilder()
  .withUrl("https://{host}/api/portal/chat"
         + "?apikey=" + encodeURIComponent(apiKey))
  .withAutomaticReconnect()
  .build();

hub.on("ReceiveMessage", c => { /* same handlers as example 1 */ });
hub.on("MarkMessagesRead", r => { /* … */ });

await hub.start();
```

#### Example 3 — contact-scoped (one thread, no AeonPass account needed)
Add `contactId` and this connection receives that
contact's thread and nothing else. Get the `contactId` from
`GET /api/portal/conversations/contact/{guestId}` or from the `contact.id` of any
conversation read.

```js
// Both parameters in the query string; the key may equally be sent as a header here.
const url = "https://{host}/api/portal/chat"
  + "?apikey=" + encodeURIComponent(apiKey)
  + "&contactId=" + contactId;

const hub = new signalR.HubConnectionBuilder()
  .withUrl(url)
  .withAutomaticReconnect()
  .build();

// From this seat the ORGANIZATION is the other side, so the test inverts.
hub.on("ReceiveMessage", c => {
  if (c.lastMessage.isFromOrganization) thread.append(c.organizationName, c.lastMessage);
  else thread.confirmSent(c.lastMessage.id);          // our own send, echoed back
});

// readByContact is false on this shape: the organization read what the contact sent.
hub.on("MarkMessagesRead", r => thread.markSeen(r.id, r.readDate));

await hub.start();
// A 401 at negotiate with a valid key means this contactId is not one of yours.
```

Replying from this seat is an HTTP call, not a hub call:

```js
await fetch("https://{host}/api/portal/conversations/send-message", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "X-API-KEY": apiKey },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    conversationId,
    sendFrom: "Contact",      // omit, or "Organization", to send as the organization
    contactId,                // required by sendFrom: "Contact"; must be this thread's contact
    messageBody: "on my way",
  }),
});
```

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: Per-organization API key. Accepted in the query string on this path only, because a SignalR handshake cannot set the `X-API-KEY` header. Optional: send the header instead wherever your client supports it, which also keeps the key out of the Azure SignalR Service redirect URL.

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: Optional. Narrows the connection to one contact's thread instead of the whole organization: the connection joins `contact-{contactId}` rather than `org-{organizationId}`, and receives that conversation only. Must be a contact of the key's own organization — anything else fails the negotiate request with a 401 rather than falling back to the organization-wide subscription. Query string only, on this path only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Connection id returned by the preceding `/negotiate` call. Set by the SignalR client, not by hand.

101.description: Switching Protocols — the WebSocket connection is established. Messages then flow as SignalR frames rather than HTTP responses.

401.description: Missing, unknown or revoked API key — or a `contactId` that is malformed, unknown, or a contact of a different organization.

post.summary: Start a conversation with a contact.
post.description:
Opens the conversation between the API key's organization and a contact.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- Get-**or**-create: a conversation is identified by (organization, contact), so calling this
  twice for the same contact returns the existing thread rather than creating a duplicate.
- `contactId` identifies a **contact**. Contacts are managed in the Organization service —
  create them with `POST /portal/contact`, or turn an event guest id into a contactId with
  `GET /portal/conversations/contact/{guestId}`.
- The contact must belong to the API key's organization; one from another organization is
  rejected with `ORGANIZATION_ID_MISMATCH`.
- A contactId that chat has not replicated yet returns a retryable
  `CONTACT_NOT_SYNCED` error — contacts arrive from the Organization service within seconds, so
  retry briefly. The same code answers an id that never existed, so give up after a few attempts.

**Response:** the conversation, whose `id` is what the send-message and message-list endpoints
take. A freshly created one has `lastMessage` null and `unreadCount` 0.

200.description: The conversation, existing or newly created.

400.description: Validation error — `errors[].errorCode` is `CONTACT_NOT_SYNCED` (unknown or not-yet-replicated contact) or `ORGANIZATION_ID_MISMATCH` (contact of another organization).

500.description: Unexpected error while creating the conversation.

get.description:
Returns a paginated page of the conversation's messages, both sides of the exchange, newest
first (`messageDate` descending).

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- The conversation must belong to the API key's organization; any other id returns
  `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED`, and an unknown id returns `404`.
- `isFromOrganization` tells the two sides apart, and it is derived from **who the message is
  from**, never from which surface recorded it. `false` therefore covers every contact-side
  message alike: an SMS reply captured from Twilio, a send from the contact's own app, and one an
  integration recorded with `sendFrom: "Contact"` on `POST /portal/conversations/send-message`.
- `senderId` follows from that: a user id on an organization-side message, and the **contactId**
  on a contact-side one. `sender` carries the display block either way, so prefer it for
  rendering.
- `isRead` is the receipt for the organization side: on a message you sent it turns true once the
  contact has read past it; messages from the contact are always `true`.
- `EventId` is a plain filter on the message's own tag — it narrows the page to that event's
  exchange, on both sides. Untagged messages (inbound SMS above all) drop out, and an event id
  that matches nothing returns an empty page rather than an error.
- `SearchTerm` matches the message body (case-insensitive substring).
- Attachments are returned inline on each message; they follow their message's visibility.

**Response shape:**
```json
{
  "data": [ ... ],
  "pagination": { "totalCount": 100, "page": 1, "pageSize": 20, "totalPages": 5 }
}
```
If `PageNo`/`PageSize` are omitted they default to `1`/`100`.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: The conversation to read. Must belong to the API key's organization.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Optional filter: return only the messages tagged to this event (both sides of the exchange). Untagged messages, inbound SMS included, are excluded.

parameters.name: searchTerm
parameters.description: Free-text filter matched against the message body (case-insensitive substring).

200.description: A page of the conversation's messages.

400.description: Validation error — `errors[].errorCode` is `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED` (the conversation belongs to another organization).

404.description: No active conversation with this id.

get.description:
Returns a single conversation with its contact, last message and unread count.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- Only conversations belonging to the API key's organization are readable; any other id returns
  `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED`, and an unknown id returns `404`.
- `unreadCount` and the read/seen flags are computed for the organization owner (the acting user
  behind the API key), so they move when the key marks a thread read. They are the
  **organization's** view of the thread on either side of it: a message recorded with
  `sendFrom: "Contact"` is incoming, so it raises `unreadCount` rather than clearing it.
- `lastMessage` is a preview of the newest message only — page the thread with
  `GET /portal/conversations/{conversationId}/messages`. It is null on a thread with no messages.
- `participants` holds the contact block alone; organization-side users are never stored as
  participants. Use `contact` / `contactId`.
- `callerRole` is always `ORG_MEMBER` on this surface.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The conversation to read. Must belong to the API key's organization.

400.description: Validation error — `errors[].errorCode` is `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED` (the conversation belongs to another organization).

404.description: No active conversation with this id.

500.description: Unexpected error while loading the conversation.

put.description:
Marks every message in the conversation read as of now, on the organization side.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- The conversation must belong to the API key's organization; any other id returns
  `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED`, and an unknown id returns `404`.
- The read state is recorded for the organization **owner** (the acting user behind the API key),
  so this also clears the badge the owner sees in the web app. Reading through the API and reading
  in the app are the same read state — worth knowing before wiring this into an automation.
- Idempotent, and the recorded time only moves forward: calling it again simply advances the read
  mark to now.
- The contact side is notified in real time (`MarkMessagesRead`) so their "seen" tick updates, on
  both channels that can reach them: their linked user account on `/chat`, and a `/portal/chat`
  subscriber connected as this contact (`?contactId=`). The second is the only one that reaches a
  contact with **no** registered account — before it existed such a contact got no receipt at all.
- Other members of the organization are not notified; they reconcile on their next fetch.

**This is the organization's read mark — there is no contact-side equivalent here.** It records
the *organization* as the reader whichever way your connection is scoped, so a contact-facing
integration must not call it to represent the person reading: that would clear the organization's
own badge. The contact side records a read only through their own app on the token surface.

**Response:** `{ "id": "...", "readDate": "..." }`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The conversation to mark read. Must belong to the API key's organization.

200.description: The conversation id and the read timestamp that was recorded.

400.description: Validation error — `errors[].errorCode` is `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED` (the conversation belongs to another organization).

404.description: No active conversation with this id.

500.description: Unexpected error while marking the conversation read.

get.summary: Resolve a guest id to a contact.
get.description:
Turns an **event guest id** into the **contactId** that the conversation endpoints take, so an
integration holding a guest id does not need the person's phone or email to start a chat.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- The guest must belong to an event of the API key's organization; guests of any other
  organization return `404`.
- The guest is matched to a contact by exact **phone**, otherwise by case-insensitive **email** —
  guest ids and contact ids are unrelated.
- A guest for whom no contact record exists returns `404`. That can be permanent (the guest was
  never synced as a contact) or transient (replication lag), and the two are indistinguishable —
  so retry briefly, then give up.

**Response:** the contact. Its `id` is the `contactId` that the rest of the portal surface takes,
and this endpoint is the usual place to get one:

| Where | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /portal/conversations/with-contact/{contactId}` | open (or, with `IsCreateNew`, start) the thread |
| `POST /portal/conversations` | start the thread |
| `POST /portal/conversations/send-message`, with `sendFrom: "Contact"` | record a message **from** this contact |
| `wss://…/portal/chat?apikey=…&contactId={contactId}` | subscribe to this contact's thread alone |

`userId` is null for a contact who has never registered. That limits **outbound delivery** — no
in-app push, so SMS/email only — but not the surface above: all four rows work for a contact with
no account, which is what they are for.

parameters.name: guestId
parameters.description: The event guest to resolve. Must be a guest of an event of the API key's organization.

404.description: No contact matches this guest, or the guest is not in the key's organization.

500.description: Unexpected error while resolving the guest.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of the API key's organization's conversations, newest activity first,
each with its contact, last message and unread count.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- Scoped to the API key's organization. There is no way to widen it — no organization or view
  parameter is accepted.
- Ordered by last activity (`updatedOn`, falling back to `createdOn`), descending.
- `SearchTerm` matches either side of the conversation: the contact's name, email or phone, and
  the organization's name, email or phone. Case-insensitive substring; a term with 3+ digits also
  matches phone numbers ignoring formatting.
- `IsUnreadOnly=true` keeps only conversations whose `unreadCount` is greater than zero.
- `unreadCount` is computed for the organization owner (the acting user behind the API key), and
  counts only messages sent after the owner joined the organization.
- `lastMessage` is null on a conversation that has no messages yet.
- `callerRole` is always `ORG_MEMBER` on this surface.

**Response shape:**
```json
{
  "data": [ ... ],
  "pagination": { "totalCount": 100, "page": 1, "pageSize": 20, "totalPages": 5 }
}
```
If `PageNo`/`PageSize` are omitted they default to `1`/`100`. A page past the end returns an
empty `data` with the same `pagination.totalCount`.

parameters.name: searchTerm
parameters.description: Free-text filter matched against either side of the conversation: the contact's name, email and phone, and the organization's name, email and phone. Case-insensitive substring; phone also matches ignoring formatting.

parameters.name: isUnreadOnly
parameters.description: Keep only conversations with a non-zero unread count. Defaults to false.

200.description: A page of the organization's conversations.

post.summary: Send a message in a conversation, from the organization or from its contact.
post.description:
Records a message in a conversation and hands it off for delivery on the channels you select.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Which side the message is from:** `SendFrom` — `Organization` (the default) or `Contact`.

| `SendFrom` | Stored as | Delivery | `ContactId` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Organization` | from the organization **owner**, the acting user behind an API key — the message appears in the web app as though the owner sent it, and the thread is marked read for them | the channels below dispatch to the contact | ignored |
| `Contact` | from the contact, exactly as an SMS reply is (`isFromOrganization: false`) | the channels below dispatch **nothing** — an incoming message notifies the organization instead | **required** |

`SendFrom=Contact` lets one key mirror both halves of a thread — an integration that owns the
contact-facing surface can record the person's replies without a user account for them. It changes
only *attribution*: the key still has to be allowed to write to the conversation, and the contact
is never a way to reach a conversation the key could not already reach.

**`SendFrom=Contact` validation** — all of it, before anything is stored:
- `ContactId` is required (`CONTACT_ID_REQUIRED`).
- It must be **this conversation's** contact (`CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED` on `contactId`) — a
  conversation is the pair (organization, contact) and has no other participant.
- That contact must exist in chat's replica (`CONTACT_NOT_SYNCED`) and belong to the API key's
  organization (`ORGANIZATION_ID_MISMATCH`). A contact of another organization can never be
  borrowed as a sender.
- Unread is not cleared for the organization: an incoming message raises the organization's
  `unreadCount`, and the response reflects that. Sending as the organization still marks the
  thread read for the owner, as before.

**Behavior:**
- The conversation must belong to the API key's organization; any other id returns
  `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED`, and an unknown id returns `404`.
- `MessageBody` and `Attachments` are both optional, so either alone is a valid message.
- `Attachments` take the values returned by `POST /portal/conversations/upload-docs`.
- `EventId` tags the message to one of this organization's events. Optional; a message needs no
  event. An event belonging to a **different** organization is rejected
  (`ORGANIZATION_ID_MISMATCH`); an id not yet replicated into chat is accepted and stored as the
  tag.
- Delivery is asynchronous: the request succeeds once the message is persisted and queued,
  independent of whether SMS/email delivery ultimately succeeds.
- The message is pushed live to every `/portal/chat` subscriber of this organization, to a
  `/portal/chat` subscriber connected as this conversation's contact (`?contactId=`), and to the
  web/member apps — regardless of the delivery channels below, and whichever side sent it. Those
  channels govern outbound delivery to the person, not who can see the message.

**Delivery channels:** all default to `false`. Set none and the message is still stored and
pushed live, but nothing is dispatched to the contact. They are only meaningful when `SendFrom`
is `Organization`: they describe how to reach the *contact*, so on a `SendFrom=Contact` send they
are stored on the row but dispatch nothing.

| Field | Channel |
|-------|---------|
| `InApp` | In-app push — reaches only a contact with a registered user account |
| `InSMS` | SMS — the one channel that reaches a contact with no account, and the channel their replies come back on |
| `InEmail` | Email |

**Request examples**

Sending as the organization — `sendFrom` may be omitted entirely, which is what every caller did
before it existed:

```json
{
  "conversationId": "3f1c…",
  "messageBody": "Your table is ready.",
  "inSMS": true
}
```

Recording the contact's reply. `contactId` is required here and must be this conversation's own
contact; the delivery channels are left off because they would dispatch nothing:

```json
{
  "conversationId": "3f1c…",
  "sendFrom": "Contact",
  "contactId": "a94e…",
  "messageBody": "On my way."
}
```

`sendFrom` is sent **by name** — `"Organization"` or `"Contact"`. The numeric form (`0`, `1`) also
binds, which is what the auto-generated example above shows, but prefer the name.

**Response:** the conversation, with `lastMessage` set to the message just sent. On a
`sendFrom=Contact` send, `lastMessage.isFromOrganization` is `false` and `lastMessage.senderId` is
the contactId.

200.description: The conversation, with the sent message in `lastMessage`.

400.description: Validation error — `errors[].errorCode` is `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED` (the conversation belongs to another organization, or `contactId` is not this conversation's contact), `ORGANIZATION_ID_MISMATCH` (the `eventId` or the `contactId` belongs to another organization), `CONTACT_ID_REQUIRED` (`sendFrom` is `Contact` with no `contactId`) or `CONTACT_NOT_SYNCED` (the contact is not yet replicated into chat).

404.description: No active conversation with this id.

500.description: Unexpected error while saving the message.

post.description:
Uploads one or more files to storage and returns their URLs, ready to be passed as `Attachments`
on `POST /portal/conversations/send-message`.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- `multipart/form-data`, field name `File`; repeat the field to upload several files in one
  request. A request carrying no file fails.
- Uploading does not attach anything to a conversation on its own — send the returned
  `url` / `fileName` / `fileType` / `storageFileName` values with the message.
- Not conversation-scoped: an upload is not bound to a thread until a message references it, and
  any conversation of this organization can then use it.

**Response:** one entry per **successfully** stored file, in upload order. A file that fails to
store is left out, so compare the response length with the number of parts you sent.

200.description: One entry per stored file, ready to send as an attachment.

500.description: No file was supplied, or storing the upload failed.

get.summary: Get the conversation with a contact.
get.description:
Looks up the conversation between the API key's organization and a contact **by contactId**, so an
integration that only stores contact ids does not have to remember conversation ids.

**Authentication:** Include `X-API-KEY` in the request header.

**Behavior:**
- `IsCreateNew=false` (default) is get-only: no conversation yet returns `404`.
- `IsCreateNew=true` opens one if it does not exist, exactly like `POST /portal/conversations`.
- The contact must belong to the API key's organization; one from another organization returns
  `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED`.
- A contactId chat has not replicated yet returns the retryable `CONTACT_NOT_SYNCED` error.
- The response is the same conversation shape the other reads return, so a single call can both
  resolve the id and render the thread header.

This is the usual entry point for an integration: guest id → `contactId`
(`GET /portal/conversations/contact/{guestId}`) → this call with `IsCreateNew=true` → send.

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: The contactId to open the conversation with. Must be a contact of the API key's organization.

parameters.name: isCreateNew
parameters.description: Create the conversation if it does not exist yet (get-or-create).

400.description: Validation error — `errors[].errorCode` is `CONTACT_NOT_SYNCED` (unknown or not-yet-replicated contact) or `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED` (contact of another organization).

404.description: No conversation with this contact yet, and `IsCreateNew` was false.

500.description: Unexpected error while resolving the conversation.

PortalCreateConversationEndpointRequest.description: Which contact to open a conversation with. The organization is always the API key's own.

contactId.description: The contactId to open a conversation with. Must be a contact of the API key's organization.

ConversationDto.description:
A conversation between an organization and one of its contacts, rendered for the calling user:
unreadCount, isReadByUser and lastMessage are all per-caller.

id.description: Conversation id — the value the send-message, message-list and mark-read endpoints take.

updatedOn.description: Last activity (UTC) — touched on every send. Null until the first message. Lists are ordered by this, falling back to createdOn.

participants.description: The conversation's participants: exactly the contact block, or empty when the contact row is missing. Organization-side users are never stored as participants — use contact.

isReadByUser.description: Read state of lastMessage from the caller's side — the same value as lastMessage.isRead. Null when the conversation has no message the caller can see.

unreadCount.description: Messages the caller has not read yet: sent by the other side, newer than the caller's last read, and not older than the caller's membership of the organization.

lastMessage.description: The most recent message the caller can see, for list previews. Null when nothing has been sent yet.

recipientUserIds.description: The contact's linked user id, when they have one; empty otherwise. These are the users a real-time push is addressed to.

organizationId.description: The organization that owns the conversation.

organizationName.description: The owning organization's display name (organizations_copy.organizationname), so the org side can be rendered — especially for CONTACT callers — without a second lookup.

organizationLogoUrl.description: The owning organization's logo URL (organizations_copy.logourl). Null when the org has no logo set.

organizationIsSetup.description: Whether the owning organization has completed setup (organizations_copy.issetup). Null when the org row is not in the replica yet. When false, clients fall back to the owner's identity instead of the org name.

organizationEmail.description: The owning organization's contact email (organizations_copy.email). Null when unset or not replicated yet.

organizationPhone.description: The owning organization's contact phone (organizations_copy.phone). Null when unset or not replicated yet.

contactId.description: The contact this conversation is with. Together with organizationId it identifies the conversation.

contact.description: The contact's display block (name, avatar, phone/email, linked user, last read).

callerRole.description:
How the caller relates to this conversation: ORG_MEMBER, CONTACT or
EVENT_MEMBER — one list page can mix roles. Always ORG_MEMBER on the X-API-KEY
surface. Null when resolved outside a caller context (the anonymous Twilio push).

PortalPagedResponseOfMessageDto.description:
Standard offset/page-based pagination shape for the portal (API key) surface, so every Portal list
endpoint returns the same { data, pagination } contract regardless of what shape the underlying
business-layer response happens to use. Same contract as the AeonPassEvent / AeonPassOrganization
portal surfaces, so one API consumer sees one pagination shape across all of them.

data.description: The items on the requested page. Empty when the page is past the end of the result set.

pagination.description: Where this page sits in the full result set.

PortalMarkAsReadConversationEndPointResp.description: Confirmation of the read mark that was recorded for the organization side.

id.description: The conversation that was marked read.

readDate.description: The read timestamp recorded (UTC) — every message sent up to this instant now counts as read.

ContactDto.description:
The person side of a conversation, projected from the contacts_copy replica. Contacts are
owned by the Organization service; chat only reads them.

id.description: Contact id — the contactId the conversation endpoints take as their target.

lastName.description: Contact's last name. Null when not recorded.

phone.description: Contact's phone number — the SMS delivery address, and the first key a guest is matched on.

email.description: Contact's email address — the email delivery address, and the fallback guest match key (case-insensitive).

userId.description: The AeonPass user account linked to this contact. Null when they have never registered — such a contact is reachable by SMS/email only, never by in-app push.

profilePicture.description: URL of the contact's profile image (contacts_copy.profileurl). Null when unset.

organizationId.description: The organization this contact belongs to. A conversation is identified by (organization, contact).

PortalPagedResponseOfConversationDto.description:
Standard offset/page-based pagination shape for the portal (API key) surface, so every Portal list
endpoint returns the same { data, pagination } contract regardless of what shape the underlying
business-layer response happens to use. Same contract as the AeonPassEvent / AeonPassOrganization
portal surfaces, so one API consumer sees one pagination shape across all of them.

data.description: The items on the requested page. Empty when the page is past the end of the result set.

pagination.description: Where this page sits in the full result set.

PortalSaveMessageEndPointRequest.description: A message to send into one of the API key organization's conversations, from either side.

conversationId.description: The conversation to send into. Must belong to the API key's organization.

sendFrom.description:
Which side the message is from: Organization (the default) or Contact. Omit it and the
message is attributed to the organization exactly as before.

contactId.description:
The contact the message is from. Required when SendFrom is Contact, and must be this
conversation's own contact, in the API key's organization. Ignored when sending as the organization.

eventId.description: Optional: tag the message to one of the organization's events. An event owned by another organization is rejected.

messageBody.description: The message text. Optional — omit it to send attachments only.

attachments.description: Files to attach, using the values returned by upload-docs. Empty by default.

inApp.description: Deliver as an in-app push. Only reaches contacts who have a registered user account.

inSMS.description: Deliver by SMS. This is the channel the contact replies on.

PortalSaveMessageEndPointResponse.description: The conversation after the send, with lastMessage set to the message just sent.

id.description: Conversation id — echoes the request's conversationId.

organizationId.description: The organization that owns the conversation — the API key's own.

organizationLogoUrl.description: The organization's logo URL. Null when none is set.

organizationIsSetup.description: Whether the organization has completed setup. Null when the org row is not in the replica yet.

organizationEmail.description: The organization's contact email. Null when unset.

organizationPhone.description: The organization's contact phone. Null when unset.

contactId.description:
The contact on the other side of this conversation. The message's recipient on a
sendFrom=Organization send, and its sender on a sendFrom=Contact one.

contact.description: The contact's display block (name, avatar, phone/email, linked user, last read).

updatedOn.description: Last activity (UTC) — this send has just touched it.

isReadByUser.description:
Read state of lastMessage, from the organization's seat.

sendFrom=Organization: false immediately after the send — it turns true
once the contact has read past the message.
sendFrom=Contact: true. The message is incoming, and an incoming message
is one you can already see.

unreadCount.description:
Unread messages for the organization owner — the acting user behind the API key.

sendFrom=Organization: 0. Sending marks the thread read for the
sender.
sendFrom=Contact: not cleared, and normally 1 or more. The message
is incoming, so it counts against the organization exactly as a real reply does — clearing the badge
here would hide a message nobody on that side has seen.

lastMessage.description: The message that was just sent, with its id, timestamp, attachments and event tag.

PortalUploadDocsEndPointRequest.description: The multipart/form-data body of an attachment upload.

file.description: The files to upload, as multipart/form-data parts named File. Repeat the field to upload several in one request; at least one is required.

PortalUploadDocsEndPointResponse.description: One uploaded file. Pass these values straight through as an attachments entry on send-message.

id.description: Id assigned to the file. Pass it back as the attachment's id when sending the message.

url.description: Public URL of the stored file. Required when sending the attachment.

fileName.description: The original file name, echoed from the upload.

fileType.description: MIME content type detected from the upload (for example image/png).

storageFileName.description: The name the file is stored under in blob storage ({id}{extension}) — unique, unlike fileName.

ConversationParticipantDto.description:
Display shape for a participant on a conversation — the contact (via
conversations.contactid) or an org-side message sender (resolved from
users_copy). Not a persisted row: the chat model has no participants table, so this is
purely a projection for the UI. "Participant" (not "member") because a conversation has both an
organization member side and a contact side; isContact tells them apart.

id.description: The contact id (contacts_copy.id) for the contact side; null for org-side senders.

conversationId.description: The conversation this participant block belongs to.

firstName.description: First name — the contact's, or the sending user's for an org-side sender.

lastName.description: Last name. Null when not recorded.

profilePicture.description: URL of the profile image. Null when unset.

lastReadOn.description: When this participant last read the conversation (UTC). Populated for the contact block only, and null until they have read it at least once.

userId.description: The linked user account: the contact's, when they have registered, or the sending user's on the org side. Null for a contact with no account.

isContact.description: True for the contact (person) side; false for an organization-member side.

MessageDto.description:
One message in a conversation. isRead is per-caller; the rest is the stored row plus
the sender's display block.

conversationId.description: The conversation this message belongs to.

senderId.description: Who sent it: the sending user's id on the organization side; on the contact side either the contact's linked user id (app send) or the contactId itself (inbound SMS, which has no user).

messageBody.description: The message text. Null or empty for an attachment-only message.

messageDate.description: When the message was sent (UTC). Messages are returned newest first, and read receipts compare against this.

sender.description: The sender's display block — resolved from users_copy for an organization sender, or the conversation's contact block for a contact sender.

attachments.description: Files attached to this message. Empty when there are none.

inApp.description: In-app push was requested for this message. Delivery channels only — they never affect who can read the message in the API or in the app.

inSMS.description: SMS delivery was requested for this message.

inEmail.description: Email delivery was requested for this message.

isRead.description: Read receipt from the caller's side: for a message the caller sent, true once the other side has read past it; always true for a message the caller received.

eventId.description: The event this message is tagged to, when it was sent in the context of one. Null for an untagged message — inbound SMS is always untagged.

eventName.description: Title of the eventId event (events_copy.title), for display. Null when the message is untagged or the event is not in the replica.

isFromOrganization.description:
True when the organization sent the message, false for the contact's own messages — SMS replies
captured from Twilio included. This is what tells the two sides of the thread apart and drives
message alignment in the UI.

PortalPagination.description: Page metadata returned alongside every Portal list result.

totalCount.description: Total items matching the request across all pages.

page.description: The page returned, 1-based. Echoes the requested pageNo, or the default when it was omitted or not positive.

pageSize.description: Items per page. Echoes the requested pageSize, or the default when it was omitted or not positive.

totalPages.description: Number of pages at this page size; 0 when there are no results.

MessageSendFrom.description:
Which side of an Org↔Contact conversation an outgoing message is attributed to — i.e. whose id is
written to messages.senderid, which is what the whole model derives "which side sent it" from
(senderid vs the conversation's contactid / the contact's linked userid).

It selects the *attribution*, never the *authorization*: the caller still has to be allowed to write
to the conversation on its own merits. Only the X-API-KEY (organization) surface may choose
, so an integration can mirror both sides of a thread through one key — a
person's token has no legitimate use for it (an org member picking it would be impersonating their
own contact, and a contact already sends as themselves).


Serialized by **name** ("Organization" / "Contact"), not by ordinal: this is a public
integration contract, and a magic number in a request body is the kind of thing a caller gets wrong
silently. The converter still accepts the numeric form on read, so 0/1 also bind. It is
applied to this type alone — the pre-existing enums on the wire keep the format their consumers
already depend on.

PortalMessageAttachmentRequest.description: An attachment on an outgoing message — the response of POST /portal/conversations/upload-docs, passed back verbatim.

id.description: The upload's id. Optional — a new id is generated when the attachment is stored either way.

fileName.description: The original file name, for display and download.

fileType.description: MIME content type, so clients can render the attachment.

url.description: Public URL of the uploaded file. Required — this is what recipients open.

storageFileName.description: The upload's storageFileName (the blob's unique name).

MessageAttachmentDto.description:
A file attached to a message. The upload endpoint returns this shape before the file belongs to a
message; the same shape comes back on every message once it has been sent.

id.description: Attachment id — generated at upload time and reused as the attachment's id when the message is sent.

messageId.description: The message this attachment belongs to. Empty on an upload response, which is not linked to a message yet.

conversationId.description: The conversation the owning message belongs to. Empty on an upload response.

url.description: Public URL of the stored file — what a client downloads or renders.

fileName.description: Original file name as uploaded, for display and download.

fileType.description: MIME content type of the file, taken from the upload (for example image/png).

storageFileName.description: The name the file is stored under in blob storage ({attachmentId}{extension}) — unique, unlike fileName.

tags.name: Realtime (SignalR)
tags.description:
The `/portal/chat` WebSocket hub, which pushes conversation updates
to API-key consumers. It raises two server→client events (`ReceiveMessage`, `MarkMessagesRead`)
and accepts no client calls — sending always stays on the HTTP endpoints.

**How do I connect?**

| I am | Credential | Subscribed to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An integration watching a whole organization | `X-API-KEY` header, or `?apikey=` | every conversation of the key's organization |
| A contact-facing surface, for a person who may have **no** account | the same key **plus** `?contactId=` | that one contact's thread |

Documentation only — this path cannot be called from Swagger UI.

tags.name: Portal
tags.description:
Integration API for a whole organization, authenticated by a per-organization
`X-API-KEY` header rather than a user's token. These are a second
door onto the same conversations the apps use — not a separate store — so anything written here
appears in the web and member apps immediately, and vice versa.

**The organization is never a parameter.** It is resolved from the key, and no request body or
query accepts an `organizationId`. Every id you pass is checked against the key's organization, so
a conversation, contact or event belonging to another one is rejected rather than silently ignored.

**Both sides of a conversation are reachable through one key.** A conversation is the pair
(organization, contact) and holds nothing else. By default you act as the organization; `sendFrom`
on the send endpoint lets you record a message **from** the contact instead — for a person who may
have no AeonPass account at all — and `?contactId=` on the realtime hub subscribes to that one
contact's thread. See `POST /portal/conversations/send-message` and the **Realtime (SignalR)**
group.

**The usual order of calls**

| # | Call | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /portal/conversations/contact/{guestId}` | event guest id → `contactId`. Skip it if you already hold one |
| 2 | `GET /portal/conversations/with-contact/{contactId}?IsCreateNew=true` | get-or-create the thread in one call — the usual entry point |
| 3 | `POST /portal/conversations/upload-docs` | only if the message carries attachments |
| 4 | `POST /portal/conversations/send-message` | send, as either side |
| 5 | `GET /portal/conversations/{id}/messages` | page the thread; or subscribe to the hub and skip polling |

**Conventions across the surface**

- Lists return `{ data, pagination }` with `PageNo` / `PageSize` (defaults `1` / `100`) — the same
  shape the other services' portal APIs use.
- Errors carry a machine-readable `errors[].errorCode`. Branch on that, not on the message text.
  `CONTACT_NOT_SYNCED` is the one worth retrying: contacts replicate from the Organization service
  within seconds. `CONVERSATION_ACCESS_DENIED` and `ORGANIZATION_ID_MISMATCH` mean the id belongs
  to another organization and will never succeed.
- `callerRole` is always `ORG_MEMBER` here, and unread counts and read flags are always the
  **organization's** — computed for the organization owner, who is the acting user behind a key.
- Reads and writes through this API share one read state with the apps, so marking a thread read
  here clears the owner's badge there too.
